extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent law firms, and corporate sponsors
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for the National Council on Patent Practicum's Certified Patent Practitioner (CPP) credential, related CLE maintenance, partner law firm obligations, and diversity/debiasing initiatives in patent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPP credential: demonstrated experience and proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPP credential is a professional designation for those who have demonstrated experience, proficiency, knowledge, and understanding of patent drafting and prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designation is earned through involvement in the patent preparation and prosecution processes. All patent lawyers, patent agents, technical specialists, patent engineers, and other patent industry professionals are welcome to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining CPP: participation in patent-specific CLEs
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPP hosts several CLE courses per year to assist members in maintaining the CPP credential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/members should join the applicant list to receive advance notification of CLE course dates. Example CLE topics listed: 'Patent Quality – What does it mean to different entities? (Corporations, USPTO, Private Practice)', 'Leveraging Big Data to Mitigate Alice Rejections', 'Developing a Patent Portfolio Consistent with Your Corporate Strategy', 'Recruiting & Hiring Knowledgeable Patent Practitioners', and 'Addressing Diversity Concerns within the Patent Profession.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pipeline Program (PPP) diversity objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPP seeks to increase the number of women and minorities within the patent profession by fostering relationships with partner law firms that have prioritized debiasing efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner firms should have active debiasing priorities/initiatives and be willing to engage in relationships that expand representation in the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPP law firm obligations / oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified Patent Practitioner law firms have ascribed to a higher level of professionalism by taking an oath to facilitate the development and training of novice patent practitioners, increase the diversity of the profession, maintain patent-specific CLEs, and intimately align themselves with USPTO and corporate-based patent quality initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law firms seeking or holding CPP firm recognition are expected to: (1) train and mentor novices, (2) implement diversity-increasing measures, (3) provide/maintain patent-specific CLE programming, and (4) align firm practices with USPTO and corporate patent quality efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational values: promote excellence and debiasing
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPP promotes excellence in patent preparation and prosecution and describes itself as 'Champions of Debiasing in the Patent Profession.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization's standards emphasize both technical excellence in drafting/prosecution and active measures to mitigate bias within the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate & law sponsor expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate and law firm sponsors recognize the value in certification, continuous patent education for practitioners at all levels, and the need to properly train novice practitioners on the intricacies of the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors are expected to support certification and ongoing education initiatives and to value training that transmits practical, intricate knowledge of patent preparation and prosecution to new practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency areas signaled by CLE topics
rubrics_metrics.description: CLE topics indicate substantive competency/knowledge areas valued by NCPP (patent quality perspectives, data-driven prosecution strategies, Alice-related prosecution tactics, portfolio strategy alignment, and hiring/recruiting practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topic areas can be read as evaluative or curricular criteria for CPP practitioners: understanding differing definitions of patent quality, applying big data to reduce rejections (e.g., Alice), constructing portfolios aligned to corporate strategy, and participating in effective recruiting/hiring and diversity initiatives.
